figures.title: The policy and effect-consumer boundary
figures.description: Grade settings are authoritative. The host supplies observations to a pure reducer, its effects authorize adapter operations, and operation receipts return as events.

figures.title: Latest-demand preparation scheduling
figures.description: The latest requested signature shares one physical preparation slot. A preview leaves the running job occupied; its final receipt starts the newest successor.

figures.title: The three-component preparation join
figures.description: The aggregate join authorizes completion only after linear, tone, and boundary preparation retire, retaining the first error until the final receipt.

figures.title: Node output and installation policy
figures.description: Output is derived as current, preview, pending, or error. Only a full-quality installation for the current demand is allowed to render.

figures.title: Helper process lifecycle
figures.description: Startup is followed by a probe, serialized work, shutdown escalation, physical exit, and cleanup. Receipts are fenced by generation and job identity.

figures.title: Production two-bank publication
figures.description: The inactive bank is staged and packed before selector readback and delivery. Repair first closes output. Selection or delivery failure restores the old selector and fails closed.

figures.title: Immutable parameter-image publication
figures.description: This comparison strategy stages a new image before binding, committing metadata, activating, and delivering. Failed binding transactions attempt every restoration component before failing closed.

figures.title: Shared-image publication and restoration
figures.description: This comparison strategy snapshots and updates an existing image. A matching clean image skips upload and packing. Failed restoration stops before inconsistent metadata can be restored.

figures.title: Compositor supersession protection
figures.description: The production PublicationGate sends completion and reset events to this policy. Its live admission and supersession path is used by the comparison example: supersession protects a scene and epoch until a later successful completion for that scene or a quiescent reset.

figures.title: Resource adoption and retirement
figures.description: Adoption is a predicate. Disposal fences and detaches subscriptions before resource observation; deletion requires cache eviction and a fresh eligibility check.

figures.title: Observer handoff policy
figures.description: Observer installation promotes only a matching pending token. Replacement preserves the current observer until the pending installation succeeds; reset preserves the monotonic serial.

figures.title: Gesture participation in the runtime coordinator
figures.description: The runtime coordinator tracks armed, active, and deferred finishing gesture phases. Scalar policy decisions authorize transitions and release only the final participant in a node.

figures.title: Render preflight authorization
figures.description: A waiting render ticket releases only after an exactly correlated published signature. Stale generations are ignored, while current mismatches fail.
